name: Chainlink
metaTitle: Chainlink Casinos: ERC20 or BEP20, Same Volatility Either Way
metaDescription: Casinos accepting LINK over Ethereum or BNB Smart Chain, with the usual network-matching caution and a reminder that it is a market-priced token, not a stablecoin.
intro:
Chainlink's token, LINK, is best known for a role that has nothing to do with gambling — it powers price-feed infrastructure used across decentralised finance — but a number of crypto casinos accept it directly as a deposit and withdrawal option alongside the majors on this list.

Where a casino supports LINK, it is typically over Ethereum (ERC20) as the native option, with BNB Smart Chain (BEP20) offered by some operators as a cheaper alternative. As with every multi-network token here, the two are not interchangeable at the address level, and picking the cheaper network when it is available can meaningfully reduce a withdrawal's cost versus defaulting to Ethereum mainnet.

LINK is a market-priced token, not a stablecoin, and its price moves with the broader crypto market rather than tracking the dollar. A casino balance held in LINK between a deposit and a withdrawal is exposed to that movement the same way a Bitcoin or Ethereum balance would be — worth factoring in if you plan to hold rather than move funds straight through.

faq.a: No — its price moves with the broader crypto market. A balance held in LINK carries the same kind of price exposure as Bitcoin or Ethereum, not the stability of USDT or USDC.

faq.q: Which network is cheaper for LINK, ERC20 or BEP20?
faq.a: BNB Smart Chain is typically the cheaper option where a casino offers it, versus Ethereum mainnet's usual gas costs for the ERC20 version.
